deities: Vajreshwari / Bajreshwari (fierce form of Durga, 'Lady of the Thunderbolt') - worshipped as a Pindi
festivals: Navratri (Chaitra and Sharad, March-April and September-October - main festival)
Ghritmandal - week-long festival when the goddess's Pindi is covered with butter, commemorating Devi healing her battle wounds with butter at Nagarkot
Pausa Jatra, Teej-Raksha Bandhan (per adequatetravel.com - verify)

history.dynasty: Katoch dynasty of Kangra (Nagarkot); rebuilt by the government in the 1920s after the 1905 earthquake
history.period: Legendary origin attributed to the Pandavas (Mahabharata era); present structure 1920s
history.summary: Shri Bajreshwari Devi Temple (Vajreshwari) in Kangra town is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas - Sati's left breast is believed to have fallen here. Legend credits the Pandavas with founding it after Durga appeared in their dream at Nagarkot. It was once among India's wealthiest temples and was repeatedly plundered: Mahmud of Ghazni (from 1009 AD, sources say up to 5 raids), destroyed by Firoz Shah Tughlaq (1360 AD), restored by Akbar, and completely razed by the 1905 Kangra earthquake. Rebuilt in the 1920s with donations including from Sikh devotees in Amritsar; the present structure is noted for its three domes. CONFLICTS: one source (royalkangra.com) says Sati's 'toe top half' fell here, against the dominant left-breast account; reported darshan hours differ between sources (see visitor_information); the winter opening time is given as 5:30 AM (tourmet.com) vs 6:00 AM (Google listing) vs 6:30 AM (thedivineindia.com).

name: Bajreshwari Devi Temple
town_description: Kangra (ancient Nagarkot) is a historic town in Himachal Pradesh's Kangra valley, about 20 km from Dharamshala. Once the seat of the Katoch dynasty, it is a major pilgrimage hub with several Shakti temples.

travel.airport: Kangra Airport (Gaggal) is about 9-14 km away (sources vary); Chandigarh Airport is about 225 km.
travel.railway: Kangra Mandir and Kangra stations are about 3 km away (narrow-gauge Kangra Valley Railway); Pathankot is the nearest broad-gauge railhead (~90 km).
travel.road: Well connected by road; Dharamshala is about 20 km and Kangra Fort about 3.5 km away.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; March-June also fine. Navratri periods are the most auspicious but most crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily darshan; hours vary by source - Google place listing gives 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily, while thedivineindia.com gives 5:00 AM-9:00 PM (Apr-Sep) and 6:30 AM-8:00 PM (Oct-Mar) with extended hours during Navratri (verify on site).
